purpose: Glasdegib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults who are newly diagnosed but are not able to tolerate intense chemotherapy. It is used together with a low-dose chemotherapy called cytarabine to help control the cancer.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes use a signaling pathway called the Hedgehog pathway to grow and survive. Glasdegib works by blocking a protein in this pathway called Smoothened, which helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from growing. Think of it like putting a lock on a door that the cancer cells were using to multiply.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or weakness, muscle pain or cramps, low blood cell counts (which can cause anemia, increased risk of infection, or easy bruising or bleeding), nausea, swelling in the hands or feet, shortness of breath, decreased appetite, constipation, and hair thinning or loss.
warnings: Glasdegib can cause serious birth defects or pregnancy loss, so it must never be used during pregnancy — both men and women must use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after stopping. It can cause dangerous heart rhythm changes (called QT prolongation), so your doctor will monitor your heart with regular EKGs. It can also cause severe low blood counts, so regular blood tests are needed. Do not donate blood or sperm while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth once a day, every day, at about the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double up on doses.
